clue.text: Large building site conceals article

indicators.note: the site word hides the article within itself, so one piece is wrapped round the other

parts.note: a site is a place or location
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A construction site screens off some item from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large building' looks like a description of the site, but it is the definition; 'conceals' puts A inside PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is a grand residence, a synonym for a large stately building.

clue.text: Study South American country's broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is spoken over the air, so we want a word that sounds like the country's possessive

parts.note: Peru is a South American country; with the possessive it is Peru's

explanation.surface: An instruction to examine some South American nation's television output.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to read or examine carefully, a verb synonym for study.

clue.text: Ruined ancestral seat of duke

indicators.note: ruined suggests something wrecked and broken up, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crumbling family home belonging to an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: The British monarch holds the title Duke of Lancaster, and the city of Lancaster is the seat the title is named for.
explanation.definitionFit: The dukedom takes its name from the northern English city, so the city is the duke's titular seat.

clue.text: Cloth that's white or light blue one-third off put on cape

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece put on another sits above it
removing a third of a nine-letter word drops its final three letters

parts.note: Cambridge blue is a light blue, and Cambridge University teams are called the Light Blues
C is the abbreviation for cape on maps

explanation.surface: A fabric of white or pale blue, with a third trimmed, placed on a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape' looks like a garment beside the cloth, but it is just C; 'or' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambric is a fine white linen or cotton fabric, so it is a cloth noted for being white.

clue.text: Knife fight about where the cash is kept mostly

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fight word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or brawl

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a till is the cash drawer in a shop

explanation.surface: A knife fight breaks out near a shop's cash register.
explanation.walkthrough: SET-TO goes 'about' TIL, which is TILL cut short by 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a slender blade, a kind of knife.

clue.text: Youngster not in employment, education or training on the way up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.words: not in employment, education or training
parts.note: NEET is the British acronym for a young person not in employment, education or training

explanation.surface: A young person without work or schooling who is nonetheless making progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' turns NEET round. NEET is a British government term for idle young people.
explanation.definitionFit: A teen is a teenager, so a young person or youngster.

clue.text: Charles recycled source of wood

indicators.note: recycled material is processed and remade, so the name's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Charles reuses timber from somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Larches are coniferous trees whose timber is widely used, so they are a source of wood.

clue.text: Taking top off, force lock

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: stress is a physical force applied to something

explanation.surface: Someone removes a lid and forces open a lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door, but here it is hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of hair.

clue.text: Facing the bowling — out!

definitions.meaning: in cricket the batter facing the bowler is said to be ...
workers who are out are taking industrial action, refusing to work

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire's verdict on the batter receiving the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batter on strike is the one receiving the bowling; 'out!' sounds like the umpire's call but is the union's.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are fixed phrases: the cricket term for the receiving batter and the industrial term for workers withholding labour.

clue.text: 'Ring me', missing the start — call again

indicators.note: missing the start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a ring, as in boxing or a circus, is an arena

explanation.surface: A request to be phoned, minus its opening, as though someone rings back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring me' reads as a phone request, but ring is an ARENA.
explanation.definitionFit: To rename is to give a new name, i.e. to call something by another title again.

clue.text: Supreme lady holding line

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the lady's title wraps the other piece

parts.note: a peeress is a woman holding a title of nobility

explanation.surface: A top-ranking woman keeping hold of a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Peerless means without equal, so unsurpassed or supreme.

clue.text: Fake diamond is a national symbol

parts.note: a sham is something fake
rock is slang for a diamond

explanation.surface: A counterfeit gem is presented as a country's emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-leaved shamrock is the emblem of Ireland, a national symbol.

clue.text: Group of settlers pass over US city

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
NY is New York

explanation.surface: Pioneers travel a route over to an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony is a community of settlers in a new territory.

clue.text: Racehorse getting one drink after another

definitions.meaning: a steeplechase horse is known as a ...
a small drink taken straight after another, such as a beer after a whisky

explanation.surface: A horse's owner celebrates with round after round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a horse in steeplechases and a drink that follows another.

clue.text: Prisoner on good terms with officer

parts.note: to be in with someone is to be on good terms with them
a mate is a ship's officer

explanation.surface: A convict who gets on well with a warder.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is someone confined in a prison or institution.

clue.text: A comedian's accessory has fishes caught in a couple of seconds

indicators.note: caught in means held inside, so the fish go into the middle of the doubled word
a couple means two copies of the next word

parts.note: a tick is a moment or second
lings are fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An entertainer's prop involves landing fish within moments.
explanation.walkthrough: The tickling stick was the feather duster prop of British comedian Ken Dodd.
explanation.definitionFit: The feathery prop was a signature accessory of a famous comic, so a comedian's accessory.

clue.text: Cross between religious groups

parts.note: inter- is a prefix meaning between
a sect is a religious group; the plural reflects the surface reading

explanation.surface: An argument or hybrid between faiths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross between' reads as a hybrid, but 'Cross' is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To intersect is to cross or cut through each other, as lines or roads do.

clue.text: Health resort with endless fix for long-distance travellers

parts.note: a spa is a health resort

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: cement fixes things together

explanation.surface: A spa with a never-ending remedy for people journeying far.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacemen are astronauts, who travel huge distances beyond Earth.

clue.text: Certain papers harassed one with rich pile

indicators.note: harassed suggests being harried and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some newspapers hounded a wealthy person with a big estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rich pile' looks like a wealthy person's mansion; pile here is the raised surface of a rug.
explanation.definitionFit: A Persian carpet is a luxurious rug famed for its deep, rich pile.

clue.text: Have a thing about unusual doilies

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is obsessed with strange lace table mats.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a thing about something is an idiom for being keen on it, close to adoring or worshipping.

clue.text: Bête noire, fear of dogs perhaps

definitions.meaning: a French phrase for something one particularly dislikes
read literally, a hatred of pets, with dogs as an example of pets

explanation.surface: A dread of dogs might be someone's personal bugbear.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the phrase into its words: loathing directed at domestic animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet hate is a particular dislike, the English equivalent of a bête noire.

clue.text: Drink of unknown manufacture?

parts.note: a brand is a make or manufacturer's label
Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A query about a beverage whose maker cannot be identified.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on 'brand X', the anonymous product; here the unknown is Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine, a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Kind of oil for wheel

definitions.meaning: oil pressed from the beans of a plant, used as a laxative and lubricant
a small swivelling wheel fixed under furniture

explanation.surface: A lubricant recommended for a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the plant-derived oil and the swivelling wheel on a chair leg.

clue.text: Abandon wild country

definitions.meaning: to cancel or drop a plan
land covered with stunted trees and bushes

explanation.surface: An instruction to desert an untamed land.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the informal verb for cancelling and the noun for rough brushland.

clue.text: Who'll renovate antique luxury car round back of furniture shop

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the car's letters wrap the rest

parts.note: RR stands for Rolls-Royce

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a store is a shop

explanation.surface: An old Rolls-Royce is parked behind a furniture shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'antique' seems to describe the car, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A restorer repairs old objects such as antiques back to good condition.

clue.text: Things used to cook up long story

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Agas are heavy cast-iron range cookers, popular in British country kitchens

explanation.surface: Ingredients for concocting a tall tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook up' suggests inventing a story, but 'up' only turns AGAS round. An Aga is a British range cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long narrative, originally a Norse heroic tale.

clue.text: Hotly contested seat alarming liberal

indicators.note: liberal means free and loose, so the letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: An election constituency where a Liberal candidate is causing alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberal' looks like a party member but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A marginal is a constituency held by a narrow majority, hence fiercely fought at elections.

clue.text: Old music club put clergyman back in prison

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the turned clergyman goes into the prison

parts.note: can is slang for prison

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar is sent back to jail from a former nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old music club' is the Cavern in Liverpool, where the Beatles made their name; 'put' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cavern Club in Liverpool was the 1960s venue where the Beatles played, a famous old music club.

clue.text: Aristocrat and toff leading motor race in France, failing to finish

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so this piece comes first

parts.note: nob is British slang for a toff, an upper-class person

indicators.note: failing to finish means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Le Mans is the famous 24-hour motor race in France

explanation.surface: A posh driver heads the field at Le Mans but retires before the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobleman is a man of noble rank, a peer or aristocrat.

clue.text: Guard southern access point

parts.note: an entry is a way in

explanation.surface: A guard posted at a southern entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to keep watch, so a guard.
